item.neoecoprototype.simplify_structure_:
Use it on a multi-block host that is already formed.
[Shift + right-click]
Not built out: builds the shape all the way to its maximum length in one go.
Already built out: carry the L9 parts and the host becomes an L9 machine on the spot - our own L1 and eco's L4/L6 alike.
[What is swapped]
The blocks it takes out are backed up in a backup drive (right-click to take them out), and the new parts come off your inventory.
[What it costs]
A successful click eats the card - both a tier swap and a grow along the edge - and the drive it leaves turns back into one empty migration drive - which crafts straight back into a card at a crafting table, one for one, so nothing is minted. A refused click eats no card: it takes one sheet of paper and one blank pattern and prints a processing pattern that turns the parts still missing into one more work order.

gui.neoecoprototype.dissociator_catalyst: Catalyst: a permanent bonus part, never consumed
Pick an online network device and sneak-right-click it to bind it to this card; sneak-right-click a second device and the two are joined by a direct AE2 network link. The mark survives a join, so one tap on a hub and then one tap per spoke is enough. Use the group field in the manager for new links; the list shows each saved link and its live status. Sneak-right-click in mid-air to open the manager; right-click in mid-air drops the mark. The unlink card removes links from one device, while the manager can remove every link in a named group. Sneak-right-click an AE2 controller to raise that network's channel mode. Wireless links draw AE from their joined network according to this world's server config.

The device panel cannot tell you whether a link is up: a device whose own grid still has power looks alive even after its link is gone. The card's two channel numbers are the only source: when a link goes, the channels allocated to this device drop with it.
Wireless ME links are switched off in the config of this world (wireless_links), so using this card does nothing right now.
No device is marked yet, so there is no network to ask: sneak-right-click a device with this card first.

item.neoecoprototype.wireless_unlink_car: Sneak-right-click a network device and every wireless link it carries comes off at once. This card marks nothing and holds no state: whichever device you click is whichever device it clears, so picking the wrong card can no longer dismantle a hub. Links never belonged to a card anyway - they live in the world's data, and a card is only the hand.

item.neoecoprototype.migration_drive.des:
Use on a formed multiblock host that already spans its full length.
[Shift + right click]
Takes it up one rung as asked, on all three families. What is mounted stays where it was - a storage matrix in its drive, the patterns in their buses.
[This drive is the price]
It is a consumable.
[What it replaces]
The old blocks are not returned by default; set migration_drive.refund_replaced_blocks to true in the server config to have them packed into one backup drive.
[What is cleared]
The communication interface's information is lost.
item.neoecoprototype.migration_drive_cre:
Use on a formed multiblock host that already spans its full length.
[Shift + right click]
Skips the rungs in between and puts this machine on L9, on all three families.
[What it replaces]
The old blocks follow the same server switch as the rest of the ladder: not returned by default.
[Creative power]
It holds a secret of the research system.
